title: Glossopteris flora of Gondwana
summary: Glossopteris was a woody, seed-bearing shrub or tree that appeared in the Early Permian, about 299 million years ago, and dominated Gondwana through the Permian. Its fossils are found in Australia, South Africa, South America, India and Antarctica, a spread that served as early evidence of continental drift. A USGS-hosted study describes its strap-shaped leaves in the Late Permian of the Beardmore Glacier region, Antarctica.

uncertainty.note: Start from the Geological Society page; end is the RSV figure for the Permian flora fossils (254 Ma), since the Geological Society page says only that it died out at the end of the Permian. The id says 260 Ma. Years are Ma counted back from the present.

as_recorded.value: emerged in the Early Permian, about 299 million years ago
The Permian Gondwanan flora fossils are 254 million years old

where.historical_name: Gondwana, Permian, at high southern latitude; no polities exist

paleo.note: Beardmore Glacier proxy at 280 Ma, near the pole. PALEOMAP gives 87.71 S, 170.85 W; MULLER2019 does not cover 280 Ma.

importance.justification: Widespread fossil plant whose distribution supported the idea that the southern continents were once joined.
